{{Short description|Picture database on emotion and attention}}
The '''International Affective Picture System''' ('''IAPS''') is a database of pictures designed to provide a standardized set of pictures for studying [[emotion]] and [[attention]]<ref name="IAPS-manual">Lang, P.J., Bradley, M.M., & Cuthbert, B.N. (2008). International affective picture
System (IAPS): Affective ratings of pictures and instruction manual. Technical Report A-8. University of Florida, Gainesville, FL.</ref> that has been widely used in psychological research.<ref>Bradley, M. M. & Lang, P. J. (2007). The International Affective Picture System (IAPS) in the study of emotion and attention. In J. A. Coan and J. J. B. Allen (Eds.), Handbook of Emotion Elicitation and Assessment (pp. 29-46). Oxford University Press</ref> The IAPS was developed by the [[National Institute of Mental Health]] Center for Emotion and Attention at the [[University of Florida]]. In 2005, the IAPS comprised 956 color photographs ranging from everyday objects and scenes − such as household furniture and landscapes − to extremely rare or exciting scenes − such as mutilated bodies and erotic nudes.

==Normative Ratings==

It is the essential property of the IAPS that the stimulus set is accompanied by a detailed list of average ratings of the emotions elicited by each picture. This shall enable other researchers to select stimuli eliciting a specific range of emotions for their experiments when using the IAPS. The process of establishing such average ratings for a stimulus set is also referred to as ''standardization'' by psychologists.

The normative rating procedure for the IAPS is based on the assumption that emotional assessments can be accounted for by the three dimensions of [[Valence (psychology)|valence]], [[arousal]] and dominance.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Osgood|first1=Charles E.|last2=Suci|first2=George J.|last3=Tannenbaum|first3=Percy H.|title=The measurement of meaning|url=https://archive.org/details/measurementofmea0000osgo|url-access=registration|date=1957|publisher=University of Illinois Press|location=Urbana}}</ref> Thus, participants taking part in the studies that are conducted to ''standardize'' the IAPS are asked to rate how pleasant/unpleasant, how calm/excited and how controlled/in-control they felt when looking at each picture. A graphic rating scale, the [[Self-Assessment Manikin|Self-Assessment Manikin (SAM)]],<ref>Lang, P. J., Bradley, M. M., and Cuthbert, B. N. (1997). International affective picture system (IAPS): Technical manual and affective ratings.</ref> is used for this rating procedure.

===Original norms===

The official normative ratings for the IAPS pictures were obtained from a sample of 100 college students (50 women, 50 men, presumably predominantly US-American) who each rated 20 sets of 60 pictures. The rating was carried out in groups using paper-and-pencil versions of the SAMs. Pictures were presented for 6 seconds each; 15 seconds were given to rate the picture.<ref name="IAPS-manual" /> Average valence, arousal and control/dominance ratings are available for the overall sample, and with men or women broken out separately.

Normative ratings were also obtained from children ages 7–9 years, 10-12, and 13-14. The rating procedure for children was mildly adapted; among other modifications, children were tested in classrooms, given instructions in a more child-friendly language, and they were allotted 20 seconds to rate each picture instead of 15.<ref name="IAPS-manual" />

===Norms from further studies===

Researchers from institutes other than the National Institute of Mental Health have also conducted studies to establish normative ratings for the IAPS in languages other than English and cultures other than US-American culture including Hungarian,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Deak|first1=A.|last2=Csenski|first2=L.|last3=Revesz|first3=G.|title=Hungarian ratings for the International Affective Picture System (IAPS): A cross-cultural comparison.|journal=Empirical Text and Culture Research|date=2010|volume=4|pages=90–101}}</ref> German,<ref name="German-IAPS">{{cite journal|last1=Gruehn|first1=D.|last2=Scheibe|first2=S|title=Age-related differences in valence and arousal ratings of pictures from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS): Do ratings become more extreme with age?|date=2008|journal=Behavior Research Methods|volume=40|issue=2|pages=512–521|doi=10.3758/BRM.40.2.512|pmid=18522062|doi-access=free}}</ref> Portuguese,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Lasaitis|first1=C|last2=Ribeiro|first2=R. L.|last3=Bueno|first3=O. F. A.|title=Brazilian norms for the International Affective Picture System (IAPS): comparison of the affective ratings for new stimuli between brazilian and north-american subjects.|date=2008|journal=Jornal Brasileiro de Psiquiatria|volume=57|issue=4|pages=270–275|doi=10.1590/s0047-20852008000400008|doi-access=free}}</ref> Indian,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Lohani|first1=M.|last2=Gupta|first2=R.|last3=Srinivasan|first3=N.|title=Cross-Cultural Evaluation of the International Affective Picture System on an Indian Sample|date=2013|journal=Psychological Studies|volume=58|issue=3|pages=233–241|doi=10.1007/s12646-013-0196-8|s2cid=143322053}}</ref> and Spanish.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Dufey Dominguez|first1=M.|last2=Fernandez Tapia|first2=A. M.|last3=Troncoso|first3=R.|title= Adding support to cross-cultural emotional assessment: Validation of the international affective picture system in a chilean sample|journal= Universitas Psychologica|date=2011|volume=10|issue=2|pages=521–533|doi=10.11144/javeriana.upsy10-2.asce|doi-access=free}}</ref> One of these studies also included older participants (63–77 years).<ref name="German-IAPS" />

==Access==

To maintain novelty and efficacy of the stimulus set, the IAPS images themselves are typically not shown in any media outlet or publications. The IAPS may be received and used upon request by members of recognized, degree-granting, academic, not-for-profit research or educational institutions.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Bradley|first1=Margaret M|last2=Lang|first2=Peter J.|title=IAPS request form|url=http://csea.phhp.ufl.edu/media/iapsmessage.html|access-date=30 May 2015}}</ref>

== Alternatives ==

===Image sets===
A group of researchers at Harvard University has published an alternative set of images that they claim to be comparable to the IAPS in 2016.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kurdi|first1=Benedek|last2=Lozano|first2=Shayn|last3=Banaji|first3=Mahzarin R.|date=2017-04-01|title=Introducing the Open Affective Standardized Image Set (OASIS)|journal=Behavior Research Methods|language=en|volume=49|issue=2|pages=457–470|doi=10.3758/s13428-016-0715-3|pmid=26907748|issn=1554-3528|doi-access=free}}</ref> The OASIS image database consists of 900 images that have been rated on valence and arousal by a sample of US-Americans recruited via [[Amazon Mechanical Turk|amazon mechanical Turk]]. As opposed to the IAPS, all OASIS images are in the public domain. A detailed description is provided on the first author's [http://www.benedekkurdi.com/#!portfolio/project-4.html homepage].

Other alternative databases of photographic images of scenes with various kinds of affective content include:
* Besançon Affective Picture Set-adult (BAPS-Adult)<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Szymanska |first1=Monika |last2=Comte |first2=Alexandre |last3=Tio |first3=Grégory |last4=Vidal |first4=Chrystelle |last5=Monnin |first5=Julie |last6=Smith |first6=Carmela Chateau |last7=Nezelof |first7=Sylvie |last8=Vulliez-Coady |first8=Lauriane |title=The Besançon affective picture set-adult (BAPS-Adult): Development and validation |journal=Psychiatry Research |date=January 2019 |volume=271 |pages=31–38 |doi=10.1016/j.psychres.2018.11.005|pmid=30458318 |s2cid=53278185 }}</ref>
* Categorized Affective Pictures Database (CAP-D)<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Moyal |first1=Natali |last2=Henik |first2=Avishai |last3=Anholt |first3=Gideon E. |title=Categorized Affective Pictures Database (CAP-D) |journal=Journal of Cognition |date=26 September 2018 |volume=1 |issue=1 |page=41 |doi=10.5334/joc.47|pmid=31517214 |pmc=6634429 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
* Complex Affective Scene Set (COMPASS)<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Weierich |first1=Mariann R. |last2=Kleshchova |first2=Olena |last3=Rieder |first3=Jenna K. |last4=Reilly |first4=Danielle M. |title=The Complex Affective Scene Set (COMPASS): Solving the Social Content Problem in Affective Visual Stimulus Sets |journal=Collabra: Psychology |date=12 November 2019 |volume=5 |issue=1 |page=53 |doi=10.1525/collabra.256|doi-access=free }}</ref>
* DIsgust-RelaTed-Images (DIRTI) database<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Haberkamp |first1=Anke |last2=Glombiewski |first2=Julia Anna |last3=Schmidt |first3=Filipp |last4=Barke |first4=Antonia |title=The DIsgust-RelaTed-Images (DIRTI) database: Validation of a novel standardized set of disgust pictures |journal=Behaviour Research and Therapy |date=February 2017 |volume=89 |pages=86–94 |doi=10.1016/j.brat.2016.11.010|pmid=27914317 }}</ref>
* EmoMadrid<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Carretié |first1=L. |last2=Tapia |first2=M. |last3=López-Martín |first3=S. |last4=Albert |first4=J. |title=EmoMadrid: An emotional pictures database for affect research |journal=Motivation and Emotion |date=1 July 2019 |volume=43 |issue=6 |pages=929–939 |doi=10.1007/s11031-019-09780-y|s2cid=198616593 |hdl=10486/709892 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

===Other mediums===
The authors of the IAPS have developed a number of non-image alternatives for eliciting emotion such as the Affective Norms for English Words (ANEW)<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bradley |first1=M |last2=Lang |first2=P |title=Affective Norms for English Words (ANEW): Instruction manual and affective ratings |date=1999 |url=https://e-lub.net/media/anew.pdf}}</ref> and International Affective Digitized Sounds (IADS).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bradley |first1=M |last2=Lang |first2=P |title=The International affective digitized sounds (IADS): stimuli, instruction manual and affective ratings |date=1999}}</ref>
